concepts.label: Native Encryption at Rest (Couchbase Server built-in)
concepts.reused_or_minted: reused - minted earlier in this batch, encryption-overview.json, where it was placed as one of four offered options for encryption:encryption-at-rest

concepts.label: Encryption-at-Rest Key
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - the user-created top-level key this page's central mechanism revolves around, distinct from the DEKs it directly encrypts

concepts.label: Data Encryption Key (DEK)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - the lower-layer key that actually encrypts data on disk; created and rotated automatically per node

concepts.label: Key Encryption Key (KEK) role
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - the role an encryption-at-rest key can optionally take on, encrypting other encryption-at-rest keys rather than data directly

concepts.label: Master Password
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - the fallback/default mechanism for encrypting configuration, logs and audit data when no encryption-at-rest key is assigned

concepts.label: Key Management Service (KMS)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - the umbrella role that creates, stores and manages the lifecycle of encryption-at-rest keys, of which Couchbase Server itself is one implementation

concepts.label: Couchbase Server Secret Management (self-managed KMS)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - opens kms: namespace; Couchbase Server acting as its own KMS

concepts.label: KMIP-compliant KMS
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - sibling of kms:couchbase-server-secret-management, any KMS implementing the Key Management Interoperability Protocol standard

concepts.label: Encryption Key Rotation
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - periodic deactivation and replacement of DEKs and/or encryption-at-rest keys

concepts.label: Force Encryption of Unencrypted Data (REST action)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - the REST endpoint that completes the encrypt-existing-data step encryption at rest otherwise leaves undone

concepts.label: Drop DEKs and Re-encrypt Data (REST action)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - the REST endpoint that completes the decrypt-existing-data step disabling encryption at rest otherwise leaves undone

relations.subject: encryption:encryption-at-rest-key
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: minted - no existing predicate captured one key type encrypting another as its designed function
relations.evidence: Couchbase Server uses the keys you create directly to encrypt Data Encryption Keys (DEKs) which uses to encrypt the information it stores on disk.

relations.subject: encryption:encryption-at-rest-key
relations.evidence: **Other encryption keys:**You can enable an encryption-at-rest key to be a Key Encryption Key (KEK) for other encryption-at-rest keys.

relations.subject: encryption:encryption-at-rest-key
relations.object: all buckets, or specific named buckets
relations.evidence: **Buckets:**You can enable a key to encrypt all buckets or restrict it to specific buckets.

relations.subject: encryption:encryption-at-rest-key
relations.object: configuration data (in place of the master password)
relations.evidence: **Configuration:**By default, Couchbase Server uses the [master password](../../manage/manage-security/manage-system-secrets.md#setting-the-master-password) to encrypt configuration data. You can choose to use an encryption-at-rest key instead.

relations.subject: encryption:encryption-at-rest-key
relations.object: log data (in place of the master password)
relations.evidence: **Logs:**You can choose to use an encryption-at-rest key to encrypt logs. You can also use the master password instead.

relations.subject: encryption:encryption-at-rest-key
relations.object: audit data (in place of the master password) - see audit:audit-log in auditing.json for the complementary side of this fact
relations.evidence: **Audits:**As with configuration and log data, you can choose to use an encryption-at-rest key or the master password to encrypt audit data.

relations.subject: encryption:master-password
relations.object: set individually on each node, not cluster-wide
relations.evidence: You must set it on each node in the cluster.

relations.subject: encryption:master-password
relations.object: providing any real security while left at its default empty-string value
relations.evidence: Because the password is known, the encryption does not provide any security.

relations.subject: encryption:native-encryption-at-rest
relations.object: Bootstrap information; node and internal client certificates; Prometheus configuration, metric data, and tokens used to gather metrics
relations.evidence: Some configuration data cannot be encrypted. This includes:

relations.subject: encryption:native-encryption-at-rest
relations.object: Analytics log files (analytics_debug.log, analytics_periodic_dump.log), which remain unencrypted even when log encryption is enabled
relations.evidence: Logs of some services are not encrypted by NS Server.

relations.subject: encryption:native-encryption-at-rest
relations.object: existing data already written to disk before encryption was enabled
relations.evidence: However, it does not encrypt existing data in the bucket or already written system data.

relations.subject: encryption:force-encryption-rest-action
relations.evidence: You can use the REST API to force Couchbase Server to encrypt existing unencrypted data.

relations.subject: encryption:native-encryption-at-rest
relations.object: already-encrypted data, immediately after encryption at rest is disabled
relations.evidence: Similarly to enabling encryption, when you turn off encryption at rest, Couchbase Server does not immediately decrypt all encrypted data.

relations.subject: encryption:drop-deks-rest-action
relations.evidence: You can force the decryption of data by calling the REST API to drop the DEKs for a bucket or type of system data.

relations.subject: encryption:encryption-at-rest-key
relations.evidence: When you create an encryption-at-rest key, you choose which KMS you want to manage it.

relations.subject: kms:couchbase-server-secret-management
relations.evidence: You can have Couchbase Server act as a KMS.

relations.subject: kms:aws-kms
relations.evidence: This method enhances security by keeping the encryption keys stored in AWS rather than on the Couchbase Server cluster.

relations.subject: kms:kmip-kms
relations.evidence: Couchbase Server can work with any KMS that implements this standard.

relations.subject: kms:aws-kms
relations.evidence: Do not assign encryption keys managed by AWS KMS or a KMIP KMS to encrypt Couchbase Server data.

relations.subject: kms:aws-kms
relations.object: reliably low-latency cluster startup, when relied on for many encryption keys directly
relations.evidence: Using AWS KMS can also cause latency issues if Couchbase Server relies on it for many encryption keys.

relations.subject: encryption:encryption-at-rest-key
relations.evidence: By default, Couchbase Server automatically rotates DEKs but not the encryption keys it manages.

relations.subject: encryption:data-encryption-key
relations.evidence: You choose how frequently Couchbase Server rotates DEKs and (if you enable it) the encryption keys it manages.

relations.subject: encryption:encryption-at-rest-key
relations.evidence: Rotation of an externally managed encryption key is handled by the KMS that manage it.

relations.subject: kms:kmip-kms
relations.evidence: KMIP compatible KMSs have their own rotation schemes and may require you to manually rotate keys or update the key IDs in Couchbase Server after rotation.

notable_absence.finding: This page never states, in its own text, that native encryption at rest is an Enterprise-only feature. The Enterprise gate is stated only on encryption-overview.md ('Couchbase Server Enterprise has a built-in encryption-at-rest feature'), which this page's own intro paragraph does not repeat or link back to for that specific fact. A reader arriving here directly (e.g. via search or a bookmark) would read the entire DEK/KEK/KMS/rotation model with no indication anywhere on the page that it does not apply to Community Edition. Captured here via evidence_source/evidence_provenance rather than dropped.

cross_component_finding: The DEK-encrypted-by-an-outer-key pattern here (encryption-at-rest key encrypts DEKs; an optional KEK encrypts other encryption-at-rest keys; an external KMS key can sit a further layer above that) is structurally the same 'outer credential wraps inner credential' idiom the registry already records elsewhere for unrelated subsystems (e.g. mgmt-api:api-key vs. capella:cluster-access-credentials as two independently-issued credential tiers). No page states these are the same mechanism or pattern - noted here only as a recurring architectural idiom across otherwise unrelated Couchbase subsystems, not as a merge candidate.
cross_product_finding: The three per-SDK 'Encrypting Your Data' links recur verbatim here as a NOTE block, identical to their appearance on encryption-overview.md - the exact same three-line list duplicated across two sibling pages word-for-word rather than stated once and cross-referenced. Minor documentation-maintenance finding (duplicated content that will drift if updated in only one place), not a modeling finding.
